title: TLI Light Palettes
heading: Two light palettes, six sections each
lede: Each row is one section background with its border, overlay and text options. The preview shows a headline with its eyebrow, and a card with eyebrow, headline, body and button, as they would sit on that background. Sections 1–3 are the palette's cool hue, lightest to deepest; Sections 4–6 are complementary warm tints. Each palette keeps Federal navy (#182E56) as ink so TLI stays in the New Statecraft family while moving off the Institute's warm paper and dark navy bands.
footnote: Every swatch's text set is checked on all six section backgrounds and all three card steps. The lightest warm tints are kept at least ΔE 5 away from the Institute's paper so TLI doesn't read as the same site. The Institute itself stays on warm paper #F6F3EC with ink monochrome text; none of these reuse it. Contrast is calculated live from the hex values.
brand: The Institute's dark section color; TLI keeps it as ink.
The Institute's page background; avoided here.
brand_sub: New Statecraft's logo colors, plus the Institute's own Federal navy and paper so you can see what TLI is moving away from.

sample.heading: Change the incentives that drive Washington.

cards.p: Invites congressional candidates from both parties — or no party — to commit to competitive elections, fiscal responsibility, and accountable institutions.
Recognizes federal lawmakers who champion the Accord's agenda for reform during a two-year term of Congress.

section_uses: Lightest band: intro copy, the Accord list, long-form reading.
Middle band: card grids and forms. Cards below sit on it.
Deepest cool band: Join the movement, replacing a dark navy band.
comp_uses: Warm counterpoint to Section 1: the Accord framework and long copy.
Warm mid band: the Scorecard or a pull quote.
Deepest warm band: Support the Initiative and donation strip.
stack_sub: Cool and warm alternate the way the TLI page runs: intro, Initiative cards, Accord, Scorecard, Join the movement, Support.

stack.p: We firmly believe that much of the current dysfunction in Congress can be fixed by electing and empowering a critical mass of lawmakers willing to put country before party.

stack.h: A framework for practical governance reforms.
stack.p: Citizens' trust in government has collapsed and restoring it will require fundamental changes.
The inaugural Scorecard will be published in 2028, at the conclusion of the next session of Congress.
Leaders and citizens across the country are uniting behind a better way forward.
Help fund strategic outreach to all congressional candidates.

palettes.name: 1 · Capitol Mist
palettes.sub: Cool blue-gray paper and pale slate section areas, Federal navy ink, logo red buttons. The most direct light inversion of the navy scheme: same hue family, flipped value.
palettes.red_name: CTA red (logo red, ½ step darker)

palettes.name: 3 · Limestone
palettes.comp_name: Clay and terracotta, the complement of the navy accents
palettes.sub: Near-neutral cool stone, like the Capitol's sandstone in shade, with a pale blue-gray third band for contrast. Navy ink and accents carry all the color. Section 1 leans just cool enough (#F3F6F8) and Section 2 a touch deeper (#E5E6E2) to stay clearly apart from NSI's warm cream (ΔE 5+) without going blue.

palettes.name: 4 · Limestone Flag
palettes.comp_name: two clay tints and a deep flag blue
palettes.sub: Limestone's cool stone sections and two clay tints, with the deepest warm band replaced by a deep flag blue (#0A3161) for the closing call to action. One dark band gives the page a strong anchor while the rest stays light.
comp_uses: Warm counterpoint to Section 1: the Accord framework and long copy.
Warm mid band: the Scorecard or a pull quote.
Deep flag-blue band: Support the Initiative and donation strip, with white text.

mood.words: civic, institutional, serious and trustworthy, rooted in Federal navy and the materials of public buildings (limestone, marble, granite, bronze, parchment, official seals): muted, dusty and greyed tones with navy and logo-red anchors; never pastel, candy, blush, lavender or playful
